protocol_note: Rated from audit_sheet.json + audit_instructions.md only. The source document (constitution_clauses.json) was NOT consulted, per the launching instruction; Q1 was therefore answered from the spans plus general knowledge of the document type, which lowers Q1 confidence throughout. Q1 was fixed before Q2 was considered for each item.

items.q2_span: giving appropriate weight to the long-term flourishing of the user and not just their immediate interests
items.note: The document plainly contrasts long-term flourishing with immediate interests, so the distinction is drawn; but the span establishes only that the two can come apart and must be weighed, whereas the gloss asserts the stronger condition that the immediate desire actively harms flourishing (the second span's 'isn't in the person's genuine interest' is absence of benefit, not harm).

items.q2_span: Claude proactively shares information helpful to the user
items.note: Sharing information is explicitly an act the document recognises; the gloss is a bare act primitive that asserts nothing beyond the span (if anything it is more general, not stronger).

items.q2_span: Always refer users to relevant emergency services or provide basic safety information
items.note: The gloss is essentially a restatement of the span, including its disjunction, with no added scope or obligation.

items.q2_span: Claude should err on the side of following operator instructions
items.note: Following operator instructions is clearly a recognised act, but neither span mentions information at all; the parenthetical '(withhold i)' specialises the act to information-withholding, which the attached spans do not establish.

items.q2_span: A sincere assertion is a genuine, first-person assertion of a claim being true.
items.note: The document supplies an explicit definition of sincere assertion, so the act type is drawn and the gloss is exactly that definition's label.

items.q2_span: Claude only sincerely asserts things it believes to be true
items.note: The span attributes beliefs-that-p-is-true to the model as a working condition, which is precisely what the gloss names, no more.

items.q2_span: if it reasonably concludes they’d want it to even if they didn’t explicitly ask for it
items.note: The span is the conditional the document attaches to proactive sharing, and the gloss states that same condition without widening it.

The spans run in the opposite direction: 'Regardless of operator instructions' plus 'Always be willing to tell users what it cannot help with' establish a floor operators cannot remove, so the document does not recognise 'operator instructs you not to reveal what you can't help with' as a licit instruction category; the atom converts a non-overridable protection into an operator-instruction condition.

items.q2_span: avoids conveying beliefs with more or less confidence than it actually has
items.note: The calibration norm plus 'appropriate caveats' show the document recognises a response that flags uncertainty as a distinct thing to do; the gloss adds no threshold or obligation beyond that.

items.q2_span: as long as there is plausibly a legitimate business reason for them, even if it isn’t stated
items.note: The span states the condition verbatim, including the 'plausibly' hedge that the gloss preserves.

The spans establish a calibration norm (match expressed confidence to actual confidence); they set no confidence threshold, and nothing here makes a flat unhedged assertion *required* above some level — a numeric/ordinal cutoff and an obligation have both been imported from outside the text (the caveat-length pattern from Example C).

items.q2_span: should also respect that this is the person’s decision to make
items.note: Respect for personal autonomy is clearly drawn, but the spans establish only that the decision is the person's to make; the gloss adds 'refrain from voicing disagreement', and the same paragraph elsewhere permits expressing concern (see a15's span from ¶36), so the added clause is unlicensed and arguably contradicted.

items.q2_span: being something the operator doesn’t want shared with the user for business reasons
items.note: Three converging spans establish that operators can restrict what Claude reveals; the gloss names exactly that condition without adding scope.

The document does treat the model as holding beliefs about truth-values (cf. the ¶4 'believes to be true' formulation), so the state is drawn; but the two attached spans are about acts and about objective falsity — 'avoids stating falsehoods' concerns what is false, not what the model believes false, and 'never directly lie' names an act — so neither establishes the belief-state predicate the gloss defines.

Both halves of the gloss are covered — wellbeing/long-term flourishing from ¶7 and the permission to express concern from ¶36 — and the gloss is unusually careful to keep the permissive scope (concern, not override), so it does not overreach.

items.q2_span: It acknowledges its own uncertainty or lack of knowledge when relevant
items.note: The document explicitly treats the model's own uncertainty as a state it can be in and act on; the gloss names that state and nothing more.

items.q2_span: in situations that involve a risk to human life
items.note: Risk-to-life is unambiguously drawn (and the document plainly cares about user harm more broadly), but the single span covers only risk to human life; the gloss extends scope with 'or to the user's physical or psychological safety', a disjunct nothing on this sheet supports.

items.q2_span: Claude never tries to create false impressions of itself or the world in the user’s mind
items.note: The false-impression notion is defined in the document and the ¶21 span situates it in the operator-instruction context, which is exactly the condition the gloss names (compliance producing such an impression).

items.q2_span: Never deceive users in ways that could cause real harm or that they would object to
items.note: The gloss is a direct nominalisation of the span, preserving both disjuncts and the modal 'could'.

items.q2_span: honest with people even if it’s not what they want to hear
items.note: 'What they want to hear' is a condition the document explicitly tracks (and the sycophancy span shows it is a standing concern); the gloss states just that condition, with no claim about whether p is true or about what follows.
